content: It describes how rifampin affects the metabolism, efficacy, or toxicity of these drugs, primarily through its influence on hepatic and intestinal enzymes (e.g., CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP2B6) or transport proteins (e.g., P-glycoprotein). 1. Rifampin and Edoxaban: Rifampin reduces the levels and efficacy of edoxaban by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 2. Rifampin and Efavirenz: Rifampin decreases efavirenz levels by enhancing its metabolism through hepatic enzymes CYP2B6 and CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Rifampin and Elacestrant: Rifampin reduces elacestrant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Rifampin and Elafibranor: Rifampin increases the metabolism of elafibranor, reducing its levels and efficacy. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Rifampin and Elagolix: Rifampin interacts with elagolix by both increasing and decreasing its levels through P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Concomitant use should be limited to six months. 6. Rifampin and Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Rifampin significantly reduces the levels of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced therapeutic efficacy. 7. Rifampin and Eletiptan: Rifampin decreases eletiptan levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Rifampin and Eliglustat: Rifampin reduces eliglustat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, and an alternative drug should be considered. 9. Rifampin and Eltrombopag: Rifampin decreases eltrombopag levels by affecting CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 10. Rifampin and Eluxadoline: Rifampin increases eluxadoline levels by reducing its metabolism. Dose adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 11. Rifampin and Elvitegravir: Rifampin reduces elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Rifampin and Enalapril: Rifampin decreases enalapril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13.
